all_reforms_including_excluded.description: The fiscal year 1966 budget introduced a significant increase in general account budget spending, marking a shift in fiscal policy to stimulate economic recovery. Additionally, the Financial Loan and Investment Programme (FLIP) was expanded by 25% over the initial 1965 programme to enhance public investment.
all_reforms_including_excluded.growth_orientation_rationale: The increase in budget spending and expansion of public investment are aimed at stimulating economic recovery, which supports growth.
all_reforms_including_excluded.status_evidence: Both reforms were part of the fiscal year 1966 budget and are stated to be implemented.
all_reforms_including_excluded.importance_rationale: The reforms represent a significant structural change in fiscal policy aimed at economic recovery.
all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: The most important features of the new programme were: i) a 17.9 per cent increase of initial general account budget spending over the initial 1965 budget.
all_reforms_including_excluded.cross_verification_note: The description focuses on a general increase in budget spending and public investment without specific mention of R&D funding or knowledge transfer mechanisms.
